title: A frequently-retrieved fact outranks an equal-trust, never-retrieved rival
description: Proves the retrieval-frequency reinforcement in combined_score end-to-end through the real fact_store search tool: two facts with identical trust and equivalent query relevance rank by retrieval_count, so a fact the agent actually keeps recalling floats above an otherwise-identical cold fact even with no explicit feedback.
contract_notes: Deterministic, no LLM. Both facts share every query-matching token (trust 0.6, same length) and differ only in one non-matching trailing token and in retrieval_count. combined_score applies usage_boost = 1 + min(0.5, 0.02*ln(1+retrieval_count)); retrieval_count 5000 -> ~+17% vs 0 -> +0%, which dominates the negligible content difference. If the reinforcement is removed the two tie on base relevance and the ordering is no longer guaranteed.
